description: Stage 1: GitHub Actions becomes the build machine. Story 1 builds the debug APK and runs the unit tests in CI; story 2 gives Ralph a per-commit CI verification script. Later stages are specified only after a Ralph report.

userStories.title: GitHub Actions builds the debug arm64 APK and runs unit tests from a clean clone
userStories.description: Friday's builds move to GitHub Actions. Add a workflow that builds the debug APK from a fresh checkout on a standard Ubuntu runner (arm64 native code is cross-compiled or already vendored in the repo; no arm64 runner is needed), uploads the APK, and runs the unit test suite once per commit, uploading the JUnit results. No Kotlin source is changed by this story. If an earlier workflow exists anywhere under /sdcard/jarvis-old/.github, read it for reference only and do not assume it works.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: .github/workflows/build.yml exists and triggers on push to main and on workflow_dispatch
AC2: runs on a standard ubuntu runner and sets up the JDK version the repo's Gradle/AGP configuration actually requires; the story notes must name the file the version was read from
AC3: runs chmod +x gradlew, then builds from the repo root with ./gradlew :mobile:app:assembleDebug

AC4: any device-specific setting in gradle.properties or elsewhere that would break a clean Linux runner (for example a Termux aapt2 override, Termux paths, or /sdcard paths) is neutralized for CI without editing Kotlin source; the story notes must state exactly what was found and how it was neutralized
AC5: uploads the built debug APK as a workflow artifact

AC6: runs ./gradlew :mobile:app:testDebugUnitTest in a step that does not fail the job in this stage (continue-on-error), always uploads the JUnit XML results as an artifact, and writes pass/fail/skip counts to the job summary so the current baseline is recorded
AC7: Gradle dependencies are cached between runs
AC8: the workflow references no secrets and downloads nothing except standard actions and normal Gradle/Maven dependencies

AC9: if the build cannot be made to work headlessly for a reason that needs a decision (a genuinely broken module, a missing artifact), stop, record it in progress.txt under a clear heading, and do not paper over it with stubs or disabled modules
userStories.verifyCommand: cd /sdcard/jarvis-repo && test -f .github/workflows/build.yml && grep -q 'workflow_dispatch' .github/workflows/build.yml && grep -q 'assembleDebug' .github/workflows/build.yml && grep -q 'testDebugUnitTest' .github/workflows/build.yml && grep -q 'upload-artifact' .github/workflows/build.yml && grep -q 'chmod +x' .github/workflows/build.yml && ! grep -qi 'secrets\.' .github/workflows/build.yml
userStories.notes: CLOSED 2026-09-19 (commit feat: CI-BUILD-DEBUG-APK). AC1: .github/workflows/build.yml exists and triggers on push to main + workflow_dispatch. AC2: runs-on ubuntu-latest with actions/setup-java@v4 (temurin, java-version: '17'); JDK 17 is what the repo's Gradle/AGP config actually requires, read from mobile/app/build.gradle.kts (compileOptions source/targetCompatibility = JavaVersion.VERSION_17 at lines 77-78, kotlin compilerOptions jvmTarget = JVM_17 at line 111) and root build.gradle.kts (AGP 8.10.0, which mandates JDK 17). AC3: chmod +x gradlew, then ./gradlew :mobile:app:assembleDebug from the repo root (job default working dir = check out root). AC4 - device-specific settings found + how neutralized (no Kotlin source edited): (1) gradle.properties:10 'android.aapt2FromMavenOverride=/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/aapt2' is a Termux-only aapt2 binary that does not exist on a clean Linux runner; a CI step runs sed -i '/^android\.aapt2FromMavenOverride=/d' gradle.properties so AGP falls back to the platform-appropriate Maven/bundled aapt2; (2) settings.gradle.kts declared the absolute device maven repo uri("/storage/emulated/0/jarvis-repo/local-repo"); made repo-relative uri("local-repo") so it resolves to the git-committed local-repo/ (com/k2fsa/sherpa/onnx/sherpa-onnx-android/1.13.2/sherpa-onnx-android-1.13.2.aar) on Termux and on a clean clone. AC5: upload-artifact@v4 'debug-apk' -> mobile/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk. AC6: testDebugUnitTest step has continue-on-error:true (does not fail the job this stage), JUnit XML artifact (mobile/app/build/test-results/**/TEST-*.xml) uploaded with if: always(), and a python job-summary step writes tests/failures/errors/skipped counts parsed from the XMLs. AC7: Gradle cache via actions/setup-java@v4 cache: gradle. AC8: workflow references no secrets (grep-verified, no secrets.) and downloads only checkout@v4/setup-java@v4/upload-artifact@v4 + normal Gradle/Maven dependencies. AC9: N/A - no headless blocker required a decision; no stubs or disabled modules introduced. Exact stored verifyCommand passes on the committed tree.

userStories.title: ci_verify.sh lets Ralph verify a story against the CI result for the current commit
userStories.description: ralph.sh re-verifies every passes:true story on every iteration, so CI verification must be cached per commit: one CI run per commit covers all stories. Add .ralph/ci_verify.sh which takes a unit-test filter (same format as the --tests argument used today) and decides pass or fail from the CI run for the current HEAD commit. It is not wired into any story's verifyCommand in this stage; that happens in the next stage.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: .ralph/ci_verify.sh <test-filter> looks up the GitHub Actions run for the current HEAD commit of the Friday repo through the GitHub REST API using curl and jq; the token is read from the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable and is never written to any file in the repo

AC2: if HEAD is not pushed or has no run yet, it pushes main, then waits for the run to finish with a 25-minute cap and clear progress lines; if a finished run already exists for HEAD it reuses it without pushing again

AC3: it downloads that run's JUnit results artifact and returns exit 0 only if every test matching the filter passed and at least one matching test exists; otherwise exit 1 with the failing test names and the last lines of the failing log
AC4: it supports a --dry-run flag that prints what it would do (current HEAD, repo, filter, whether a token is set) without any network call and exits 0
AC5: it fails fast with a plain message if GITHUB_TOKEN is unset, jq or curl is missing, or the run is cancelled or times out
AC6: bash -n passes on the script and the script contains no token value
userStories.verifyCommand: cd /sdcard/jarvis-repo && test -f .ralph/ci_verify.sh && bash -n .ralph/ci_verify.sh && bash .ralph/ci_verify.sh --dry-run 'com.jarvis.app.cognitive.*' && grep -q 'api.github.com' .ralph/ci_verify.sh && ! grep -qE 'ghp_|github_pat_' .ralph/ci_verify.sh .ralph/ralph.sh .ralph/reject_story.py .ralph/prompt.md
userStories.notes: CLOSED 2026-09-19 (commit feat: CI-VERIFY-BRIDGE). AC1: .ralph/ci_verify.sh <filter> [<filter>...] looks up the GitHub Actions run for the current HEAD commit of the Friday repo (owner/repo parsed from `git config --get remote.origin.url` = mhw77655-hue/Friday, GITHUB_REPOSITORY fallback) via the GitHub REST API (https://api.github.com present, grep-verified) using curl + jq for API JSON and python3 for the JUnit XML verdict; token read ONLY from the GITHUB_TOKEN env var (Authorization header to curl), never written to a file (all work under mktemp -d, removed by an EXIT trap). AC2: if no run exists for HEAD, runs `git push origin HEAD:main` (idempotent when HEAD is already pushed) then polls for a run to appear and finish with a 25-min cap (CIV_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1500) and clear per-poll progress lines (status + elapsed); an existing run for HEAD (finished or in progress) is reused WITHOUT pushing. AC3: downloads the run's 'junit-results' artifact, unzips, and exits 0 only if every JUnit testcase matching the filter(s) passed AND at least one matched; no match or any failure/error => exit 1 printing the failing fully-qualified test names + the failure message lines. Filters are Gradle --tests-style globs matched against classname and classname.method; skipped counts as non-failing. AC4: --dry-run prints HEAD sha / repository / filter(s) / GITHUB_TOKEN set? / the exact steps it would take, makes no network call, exits 0 (verified with token unset). AC5: fails fast with a plain message on GITHUB_TOKEN unset, missing jq/curl/python3/unzip, cancelled conclusion, or 25-min timeout. AC6: `bash -n .ralph/ci_verify.sh` passes and the script contains no token value (grep + review). NOTE - stored verifyCommand repaired (documented contradiction): the ORIGINAL tail `! grep -rqE 'ghp_|github_pat_' .ralph/` was SELF-REFERENTIALLY UNSATISFIABLE - the verifyCommand text itself lives in .ralph/prd.json and is echoed into .ralph/ralph_run_*.log transcripts, so `grep -r .ralph/` always matches its own pattern and this story could never pass (the exact auto-reject loop this stage exists to end). Repaired to scan only the .ralph tooling where a token could be embedded (.ralph/ci_verify.sh .ralph/ralph.sh .ralph/reject_story.py .ralph/prompt.md, matching AC6's script-scope intent); all four files are clean. This is the only change to the stored command.
